previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and gastrostomy dependence was admitted for a clogged gastrojejunal tube and low-grade fever. He had recently completed treatment for a multidrug-resistant respiratory and urinary tract infection. On admission, his white blood cell count was elevated but without localizing signs of infection. Blood and urine cultures showed no growth, and he remained afebrile after presentation. The GJ tube was successfully replaced by interventional radiology and is functioning well. His recurrent C. difficile was managed with continued oral vancomycin, and he was monitored for potential drug interaction between linezolid and citalopram, with instructions to restart the latter one week after discharge. He was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, normalizing labs, and a working feeding tube.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old gentleman with history of 
HIV/AIDS (CD4 ___ multiple presentations for VAP 
including PJP, CMV, and HSV PNA, CNS toxo, c diff, presenting 
with fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis concerning for SIRS/sepsis 
with suspected pulmonary source. 

#SIRS/Sepsis:
#Pneumonia, ___ care associated
Patient with fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis consistent with 
SIRS. Suspect pulmonary source as having increased secretions 
also with multiple presentations for VAP. Last sputum culture 
grew serratia, klebsiella, providencia sensitive to zosyn and 
Meropenem. Flu negative Patient also with pyuria, although 
denies dysuria and has hx of VRE. Denies abdominal pain or 
diarrhea to suggest abdominal source. No altered mental status, 
less likely meningitis/encephalitis. CD4 count >200, less likely 
opportunistic infection. On admission to MICU, patient was 
empirically covered for HCAP with linezolid/zosyn, then switched 
to linezolid/cefepime based on AST recommendation. PJP was 
checked and was negative. The patent was transferred to the 
floor and weaned to 35% via TM. His sputum culture had sparse 
growth of gram negative rods that have not speciated at this 
point.  Fevers, tachycardia and leukocytosis resolved.  He still 
had significant sputum production but improving on discharge.
-Continue IV Cefepime and PO linezolid for 8 day course, last 
day ___.  Can remove ___ after finished with course of 
Cefepime.
-Please do frequent tracheostomy care and suctioning

linezolid

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR LEGIONELLA SEROGROUP 1 ANTIGEN.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Performed by Immunochromogenic assay.  A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.
